transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up your time for something silly, but... well, I help plan events and conventions for work, so lately I've had to be out in front of people a lot more. And... I guess I've just been getting a little stuck on how I look in photos. 

There's this one part of my face that just looks really uneven to me. I try not to make a big deal out of it, and everyone else tells me they barely see anything at all, but... I just can't seem to stop staring at it when I see a picture of myself. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit vain, but it's been bothering me and I just felt like I should talk to someone. Is that... is it okay that I came in for that?
When you look in the mirror or see a photo of yourself, is it just that one part of your face that bothers you, or do you find yourself feeling self-conscious about other parts of your body as well?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. It's really just... just that one specific part of my face. I mean, I guess I have normal insecurities like any other twenty-year-old girl, you know? But I really try not to complain about my body or anything like that. I know I should just be grateful for my health, and I am, I promise. 

It's just... that one spot that seems so, um, glaring to me. Even though I know I shouldn't let it get to me, it just catches my eye every time. I really try to just focus on my work and my events, but it's hard when there are cameras around. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions okay... I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.

How much does this concern about that part of your face bother you when you're not in front of a camera or looking at photos? Does it stay on your mind a lot, or affect things like your work, social life, or how you feel about yourself?

Um... well, I really try hard not to let it get in the way of my day-to-day life. I pride myself on being professional and doing a good job, you know? But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it does stay on my mind a bit more than I'd like. 

I actually... I feel really embarrassed even admitting this, but I recently missed part of a planning deadline. I just... I spent so much time trying to deal with how I looked in some of the event materials that I completely lost track of time. And lately, even just doing my normal tasks, like getting ready for vendor calls or prepping for meetings... it takes me a lot longer than it should because I get so caught up worrying about it. 

I know I shouldn't let something so silly affect my work, and I feel awful about it. I really am trying to push through it and do better, I promise. Do you think... is it normal for something like this to be that distracting? I just hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should be.
When you’re worried about how that part of your face looks, do you find yourself doing things like checking mirrors, taking lots of photos, or trying to cover it up?

Oh, um... well, I guess I do a little bit of that. Just, you know, making sure I look presentable for work. I mean, it's important to look professional when you're representing an event, right? 

But... I suppose sometimes it gets a little out of hand. Like, before I send out event pictures or hop on a video call with a vendor, I might... um, I might check my phone camera a few times. Or, you know, retake a photo if the angle is bad. I try to tilt my head a certain way so it doesn't look as noticeable. And sometimes I might ask a coworker if I look okay... just to be sure I'm not overthinking it. 

I know it sounds like I'm being really high-maintenance, and I hate that. I really try not to bother people with it. But... sometimes I get so caught up in checking and making sure it looks okay that it eats up a lot of my time, and that's when I end up falling behind on my planning stuff. I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't be wasting time on something like that when I have a job to do. Is that... does that sound like something a lot of people do, or am I just being completely ridiculous about it?

When you're not looking at photos or mirrors, and there's no camera around, do you still find yourself thinking about that part of your face a lot — like it's constantly on your mind, even when you don't want it to be?

Um... yeah, I guess I do. Even when I'm just sitting at my desk or driving, it's... it's kind of just there in the back of my mind. 

I actually... I think that's why I finally decided to come in and talk to someone. Ever since I got this promotion and I have to be more front-and-center at work, dealing with clients and vendors face-to-face... it's just gotten so much harder to ignore. I keep picturing how that uneven part of my face must look to them. And then when I see the event photos afterward, I just... I can't stop staring at it. 

I know it sounds so vain, and I promise I'm not usually like this. I've even pointed it out to my friends and my sister, and they all swear they barely see anything, which makes me feel even crazier for obsessing over it. I really want to believe them, but I just can't shake the feeling that everyone is noticing it. 

I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't be letting something so small take up so much space in my head. I really am trying to just focus on my job and be a good employee. Do you think... is it okay that I came in for this? I just didn't know how else to get it to stop bothering me so much.
How much time would you say you spend each day thinking about that part of your face, even when there's nothing you can do about it?

Um... gosh, time... I'm really not sure how to put a number on it. I try so hard to just keep my head down and work, you know? I want to be productive. 

But I guess... if I really think about it, it's kind of... just a low hum in the background for a lot of the day. Like, I don't sit there with a stopwatch or anything, so I couldn't give you an exact amount of hours. Sometimes I can distract myself if an event is really busy, but then my mind just wanders right back to it as soon as I have a quiet moment. 

I don't know, is there a normal amount of time people spend thinking about this kind of stuff? I'm probably just making a mountain out of a molehill, right? I really don't want to sound like I'm completely obsessed or anything, because I really do try to focus on my work. I hope that makes sense?
How much distress or discomfort does this concern about your face cause you, and does it interfere with your ability to function in your daily life or relationships?

Um... well, it definitely bothers me, but I try really hard not to let it show or get in the way of things. I want to be a good employee and a good friend, you know? I really don't want to be a burden to anyone because of this.

But... I guess it has been affecting things a little bit lately. I actually... um, I missed part of a planning deadline recently. It was just... I spent so much time trying to fix how I looked in the event materials before sending them out, and the time just got away from me. I felt terrible about it. I really try to be on top of everything. 

And, um, getting ready for vendor calls and meeting prep... it just takes me longer than it should now, because I'm so worried about how I'm coming across on camera or in person. I just want to make sure I look professional for the company. 

I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't let it interfere with my work like that. I really am trying to push through it and do my job well. I hope my boss doesn't think I'm slacking off or anything. Does... does that make sense? I'm trying not to let it ruin my life or anything, I promise.
When you look at that part of your face, do you see it as a flaw that you believe is significant or unattractive, even though others may not notice it at all?

Um... yeah, I guess I do see it that way. I mean, I know I mentioned this earlier, but it's really the main reason I'm here. Ever since I got promoted and I have to be in front of people so much more, it's just... it's all I can focus on. 

When I look at event photos or catch my reflection, that uneven part of my face just looks so... obvious to me. It feels like this huge, glaring thing. But then, like I said, my sister and my friends tell me they don't even know what I'm talking about. They swear they barely see anything at all. 

I really want to believe them, I do. I don't want to be the kind of person who fixates on something so silly. I know it probably sounds like I'm just being totally vain and ridiculous, right? I'm really trying to just accept it and be professional, but... it's just hard when it looks so significant to me. I'm sorry, I hope I'm not repeating myself too much... I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.

Do you ever find yourself repeating certain actions — like checking your appearance, adjusting how you look, or seeking reassurance — because it helps you feel less anxious about that part of your face?

Um... well... I guess I do have a few little habits like that. I really try not to let it be a big deal, though. I just want to make sure I'm presenting myself well for the company, you know? 

Like, before I send out event pictures or join a vendor meeting, I might... um... I might just check my face in my phone camera a few times. And sometimes I'll retake a photo if it catches me at a bad angle, or I'll try to tilt my head a certain way so it's less noticeable. Just normal stuff that anyone would do to look professional, right? 

And, um, sometimes I might just casually ask a coworker if I look okay, or if my face looks weird. I really try not to bother them too much with it, I promise. I just want to be sure. 

But... I guess sometimes all of that checking and adjusting... it can take up a bit more time than I intend. Like I mentioned before about falling behind on some of my planning stuff... it's usually because I get a little caught up trying to make sure I look presentable. I really am trying to get better at it, though. I don't want to be high-maintenance or anything. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too crazy...
